name: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese Salt Cod with Potatoes & Eggs)
why: Salt cod (bacalhau) is Portugal's national fish, with 1,000+ regional recipes — and this is the beloved Lisbon café version: crisp shoestring potatoes swimming in warm, creamy egg with heaps of flaky cod. A rich, warming midwinter comfort dish where all the hard work (soaking the fish) is an easy hands-off overnight step.
ingredients: 1 pound (450g) dried salt cod (bacalhau), boneless if possible
1 1/2 pounds (680g) russet potatoes, peeled and cut into matchstick-size strips (about 6 cups)
1/2 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste

steps: Soak the salt cod in a large bowl of cold water overnight (at least 8 hours), changing the water 2-3 times to draw out the excess salt.
The next day, drain, then simmer the cod in fresh water until just tender (about 15 minutes). Drain well and flake the fish, carefully discarding any bones and skin.
Heat 4 tablespoons of the olive oil in a heavy, large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the potato matchsticks in batches and sauté until crisp and golden, about 7 minutes per batch. Transfer to paper towels to drain as you go.
Add 1 tablespoon of the oil to the same skillet. Add the onion and bay leaf and sauté until soft and golden, about 15 minutes. Discard the bay leaf.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil to the onion, then mix in the flaked cod and the crisp potatoes.
Whisk the eggs, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon pepper together in a large bowl.
Pour the egg mixture and 3 tablespoons of the parsley into the cod and potato mixture.
Cook over medium heat until the eggs are just softly set, stirring occasionally, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat while the egg still looks slightly runny — it will keep setting off the heat.
Transfer to a warm platter. Scatter over the olives and the remaining tablespoon of parsley. Serve immediately.

pro_tips: Never skip the overnight soak — it pulls out the excess salt so the finished dish isn't overpowering. Change the water a couple of times and taste a small piece before seasoning the egg.

The secret to the creamy texture is undercooking the egg: pull the pan off low heat the moment the egg is just set but still loose. Residual heat finishes it into a soft, custardy scramble rather than dry curds.
author: Henry
